A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a decentralized gradient method for a general non-convex objective function, which can tolerate delayed gradient information and is robust to random delays.
we provide the first convergence analysis of a decentralized gradient descent method with delayed and noisy gradient information.

the decentralized gradient method with delayed gradients converges to the consensus optimal solution, and the convergence rate is proportional to the inverse of the step size and the inverse square root of the average degree of the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, as long, as the random delays of the gradient information are bounded in expectation, the convergence rate of the consensus algorithm is not affected by the delays.
decentralized consensus algorithms can still converge to the optimal solution even if the gradient information is delayed and noisy.
, even when the gradient information across the nodes in a network is stale and noisy, decentralized algorithms can still converge to a consensus solution.
